terms.gloss: anniversary, a day that comes round every year
terms.comment: anniversārius is “returning every year” (Lewis & Short): yearly feasts and rites are fēstī diēs anniversāriī and sacra anniversāria in Cicero.

terms.gloss: anniversary (of the founding of a city, a colony, a temple)
terms.comment: Properly a birthday; transferred to “any anniversary, a commemorative festival” (Lewis & Short).

phrases.latin: ibi mihi Tulliola mea fuit praestō nātālī suō ipsō diē, quī cāsū īdem nātālis erat et Brundisīnae colōniae et tuae vīcīnae Salūtis
phrases.english: my little Tullia was there to meet me on her very birthday, which happened also to be the anniversary of the colony of Brundisium and of your neighbour, the temple of Salus

phrases.latin: ubi ūsque ad hoc tempus Syrācūsānī fēstōs diēs anniversāriōs agunt celeberrimō virōrum mulierumque conventū
phrases.english: where to this day the Syracusans keep a yearly festival, with great crowds of men and women

sources: Lewis & Short: anniversarius · Lewis & Short: natalis
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 271.
